changelog: [Core Principles]: added a new principle framing long multi-clause utterances as the primary latency opportunity — explicitly states that the mere presence of a continuation-marker suffix (-는데/-고/-아서·어서/-니까) must not by itself block a split when the clause before it is already a complete, independently translatable proposition. This is a philosophy-level permission (not a Decision Procedure or Never-Segment change) intended to bias the model toward the aggressive splits the critic flagged as missing, without touching the already-working carve-out logic in [Decision Procedure] or the bans in [Never Segment].

[When to Segment]: added three concrete, narrowly-scoped permissive bullets covering the three under-segmentation patterns raised by the critic — (1) split after contrastive '-는데' when both the preceding and following material already form complete subject+predicate propositions, (2) split after causal '-아서/어서/니까' when the following clause is a self-contained result/feeling statement, (3) split after a '-고' clause when the following clause carries its own conditional marker (-면/-으면). These are additive permissions layered on top of the existing rules, not replacements for the [Never Segment] bans, minimizing risk of contradictory instructions that could break output validity.
